title: Hybrid decode optimizer with confidence metrics and graceful degrade
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a runtime component that can run a low-cost, low-latency generator for the common/fast path and a higher-fidelity verifier for expensive/uncertain outputs. This reduces overall cost and 95/99p latency tail while preserving output quality and providing predictable fallback behavior.

Problem statement: currently our decode stage always runs the full model; for many prompts a smaller model or a fast kernel path would produce identical outputs and much lower cost/latency. We need a production-safe system that: (1) can pick a fast kernel+model candidate for prefill and early decode, (2) computes a lightweight confidence signal to decide whether to accept the fast result, and (3) gracefully upgrades to the slow/high-quality path (or re-decodes) when acceptance fails. The component also needs to integrate with kernel selection, KV cache reuse, and autoscaling to avoid surprising resource spikes.
technical_notes:
High-level architecture: Router -> FastSynth (small/quantized model or optimized kernel) -> Acceptance Scorer -> (Accept -> emit) or (Reject -> Validator pool triggers full-model decode/rollback).

Signals and acceptance heuristics: token-level logit alignment (top-k overlap), prefix KL estimate with cheap sampling, token entropy delta, and a rolling per-route acceptance posterior computed with EWMA. Combine model confidence with hardware kernel fingerprint (some kernels have higher numerical drift).

Kernel and KV strategy: run FastSynth on int8-quantized kernels with fused attention when available; ensure KV cache format is compatible with Validator to avoid full prefill cost on re-decode where possible. Add a compact prefill sketch (hashes of key prefixes) to detect cache reuse.

Scheduling and resource control: FastSynth jobs run on a small, high-concurrency pool with tight latency SLOs; Validator runs on reserved capacity with pre-warmed weights. Router uses predictive backpressure to avoid overloading Validator when acceptance rates decrease.

Implementation plan: prototype scorer + routing in runtime-v2, add kernel metadata to model catalog, extend trace/span to annotate acceptance decisions. Unit tests against synthetic divergence cases and A/B harness for quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can route requests to a FastSynth path and produce an acceptance decision within 15ms on average for prefill+first decode token.
End-to-end 95th percentile latency for normal workloads reduces by at least 20% when FastSynth acceptance rate >= 60%.

When acceptance fails, Validator re-decode yields output with no user-visible corruption; rollback/replace must occur within bounded time (fall-back path adds no more than 2x the baseline decode latency).
Observability: route-level acceptance_rate, rollback_rate, decision_reason, and per-model kernel_fingerprint are visible in Console and in traces.
Quality safety: on our canonical eval set the hybrid path shows no statistically significant degradation vs baseline full decode (alpha=0.05).
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. Phase 0: internal canary with low volume (5%) using recorded traffic playback.
Phase 1: small customer alpha (10% of targeted routes) with explicit opt-in and guardrails for rollback.
Phase 2: broaden to 50% with autoscaling knobs enabled and automated rollback rules for increased rollback_rate or quality regressions.
Phase 3: global enable with knobs for per-customer/route acceptance thresholds and model pinning.
Fallback behavior: immediate metric-driven disable and per-route fallback to baseline decode if rollback_rate > 5% sustained for 5 minutes.
observability_and_metrics: avg/95/99 latency for fast path, validator path, and combined
cost_per_token and tokens/sec split by path
quality-regression alerts: periodic evals and production prompt-set scoring
test_plan: Unit tests: scorer math, thresholding edge cases, kernel metadata parsing
Integration tests: simulate partial KV cache reuse and confirm Validator can re-decode from prefill sketch
Load tests: measure acceptance_rate and Validator capacity under increasing traffic; ensure Router backpressure engages
Canary QA: run production traffic replay and compare outputs using our eval harness for regressions
Chaos test: force kernel drift and simulate Validator overload to verify graceful degradation rules
open_questions: What is the best single-number acceptance score that balances cost and quality across families? (we currently prototype with prefix-KL + top-k overlap)
How to generalize KV cache sketch so Validator reuse avoids full prefill without leaking state between tenants?
Should acceptance thresholds be model-specific or route-specific? Recommend we start route-specific with conservative defaults.
Operational runbook: what automated actions should be taken when Validator latency increases due to cold starts?
decisions: Use a combined acceptance heuristic (entropy delta + top-k overlap) as the initial gate — easy to compute on-device and interpretable.
Store kernel metadata in the model catalog and use it at routing time to avoid routing fast paths to incompatible kernels.
Implement a compact prefill sketch (64-bit bloom/hash) to enable partial KV reuse for Validator without full prefill data transfer.
Expose per-route acceptance threshold as a runtime-configurable knob; default conservative value will be tuned via canary.
